# Reception Perception: The Show — 2024-02-27

**Raw transcript:** `raw/ingested/reception-perception/2024-02-27-rp-tee-higgins-mike-evans-marvin-harrison-jr-bieniemy-picks-college-ball.md` (immutable — do not edit)

## Summary

With co-host **James Koh** (not tracked). Free-agency-eligible-receiver
deep dive plus a college-football detour.

**[[Tee Higgins]].** Fresh 2023 Reception Perception charting shows a down
year across the board — career/near-career-low success rates vs. man, press
and zone, plus a career-low catch rate — which Harmon flags but hesitates to
fully hold against Higgins given he played through injury. Both hosts draw a
sharp line between Higgins and true "transformative" receivers ([[Tyreek
Hill]], [[A.J. Brown]]): Higgins is franchise-tag-worthy and "top-20-ish," but
has never proven he's a true WR1 without [[Ja'Marr Chase]], and the trade
market (Carolina's No. 33 floated) doesn't look like a bidding war. Koh
thinks Cincinnati should have pushed harder for an extension while his value
was down rather than tagging him.

**[[Mike Evans]].** The inverse — one of his best-charted seasons ever
(career-best man-coverage success rate, second-best press number). Credited
to new OC Dave Canales reshaping his route tree away from go routes and
toward slants/outs, which (per Next Gen Stats) actually produced *more*
downfield production on 20+ air-yard targets than his heavier-go-route 2022.
Framed as a technically excellent, underrated route runner miscast as a pure
jump-ball receiver. Contract projection: $18M+/year, with the Kenny Golladay
2021 deal as a floor comp and Davante Adams's Raiders deal as a ceiling comp.
Hypothetical fits discussed if he reaches the open market: Detroit, the
Rams, the Chiefs, and especially Baltimore (paired with [[Zay Flowers]] and
[[Rashad Bateman]], replacing a fading Odell Beckham Jr. role).

**[[Marvin Harrison Jr.]].** Both hosts note he's not hiring an agent and
will skip *both* the combine and his Ohio State pro day — Harmon's "antenna
is raised" more by the pro-day opt-out than the combine one, calling it a
step beyond precedent (DeVonta Smith, Jalen Waddle skipped only the combine).
Cites reported private testing numbers via Albert Breer (6'3"/206 lb, 380 lb
bench x22 at 225, 3.94 pro shuttle, 10'9" broad jump, 23 mph GPS top speed) as
evidence teams already have what they need without a live workout. Doesn't
change Harmon's own evaluation — he has no questions left that a drill would
answer — but reads it partly as narrative management by Harrison's camp.
Harmon plans top-10 grades for all three of Harrison, [[Malik Nabers]] and
[[Rome Odunze]], explicitly declining to rank them 1-2-3 against each other:
with talent this close among the trio, he expects landing spot to decide
whose career looks better, not the pre-draft pecking order — illustrated with
a 2023 example (Quentin Johnston was never as good a prospect as [[Zay
Flowers]], and getting drafted by Justin Herbert's Chargers didn't change
that). See [[Dynasty]] and [[NFL Combine and Pro Day Skepticism]].

**College football detour.** Eric Bieniemi is leaving his Washington OC job
to become UCLA's offensive coordinator under new 44-year-old head coach
Deshaun Foster. Both hosts are stunned by the move given how disappointing
Washington's offense was in 2023 (18th in offensive success rate, 25th in
EPA/play) and view it as a step down for Bieniemi's head-coaching prospects.
No standalone fantasy-relevant player evaluation here — the segment closes
with a nostalgic, non-evaluative tangent through the 2007-08 Carolina
Panthers roster (Deshaun Foster's playing career, Jake Delhomme, D'Angelo
Williams, Steve Smith Sr.).
